title: T1561 — Disk Wipe
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Disk Wipe with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.

steps.title: 1 · Phish
steps.caption: Attacker: sends an invoice-themed email with a malicious macro document; an employee enables macros and a small implant calls home.
steps.defender: a single Office process spawning PowerShell on one workstation, often buried in normal noise.

fields.detail: Attacker: sends an invoice-themed email with a malicious macro document; an employee enables macros

steps.title: 2 · Move
steps.caption: Attacker: steals credentials from the workstation, then uses them with SMB and WMI-style remote administration to reach file servers and domain systems.
steps.defender: remote execution events from one account touching many hosts within minutes, plus new logons at unusual hours.

steps.caption: Attacker: copies the wiper binary to a trusted file share and pushes it out with scheduled tasks or group policy.
steps.defender: a new executable appearing on a share and identical scheduled-task creations landing on dozens of hosts in a row.

steps.title: 6 · Crash
steps.caption: Attacker: lets machines restart into corrupted boot records; hundreds of systems cannot start.
steps.defender: unexpected reboot events followed by boot failure errors and a fast-rising helpdesk queue.

steps.caption: Attacker: has finished; the damage is now visible everywhere.
steps.defender: EDR mass-overwrite alerts, unbootable hosts reported from many sites, and the SOC declaring a major incident.

steps.title: 8 · Recover
steps.caption: Lesson: offline, tested backups turn a catastrophe into a bad week
steps.defender: segment the network to stop any remaining spread, rebuild hosts from golden images, restore data from offline backups, and rotate every credential the attacker may have held.
